wip.title: What is Padel?
wip.paragraph: Padel also sometimes called padel tennis, is a racket sport of Mexican origin, typically played in doubles on an enclosed court slightly smaller than a doubles tennis court. Although padel shares the same scoring system as tennis, the rules, strokes, and technique are different.

federation.red-text: The Padel Federation of Macedonia is the official governing body for the sport of padel in Macedonia. Established to promote, develop, and regulate padel across the country, the MPF is dedicated to fostering a vibrant and inclusive community for players of all ages and skill levels.

our-mission.title: Our Mission
our-mission.text: Our mission is to enhance the growth of padel in Macedonia by providing support and resources to players, coaches, and clubs. We strive to create opportunities for competitive play, develop talent, and ensure the sport is accessible to everyone.

join-us.title: Join Us
join-us.text: Become part of the vibrant and growing padel community! Whether you're an individual player eager to enhance your skills, a team ready to compete, or someone interested in becoming a certified coach, the Padel Federation of Macedonia welcomes you.

championship2026.intro: The Padel Federation of Macedonia proudly announces the first Open National Padel Championship, to be held on 04–05 July 2026 in Kumanovo, with technical organization by Padel Club Kumanovo.
championship2026.posterAlt: Open National Padel Championship of Macedonia 2026 poster

about.p1: This event marks a significant step in the development of padel in Macedonia and aims to bring together all lovers of the sport in one place.
about.p2: The championship is open to all interested players, while member clubs of the Federation will additionally compete for the club standings and the title of most successful club of the championship.
about.p3: With this, the Federation aims to enable maximum involvement of the padel community while also recognizing the clubs that actively contribute to the development of the sport.

recognition.title: Officially recognized federation
recognition.text: The Padel Federation of Macedonia is the only officially recognized national padel federation in the country, a member of the International Padel Federation (FIP) and the European Padel Association (FEPA).

ranking.title: Official national ranking
ranking.text: Participation in tournaments held under the Federation is the sole basis for official national player ranking. Results achieved at these competitions count toward the national ranking system.

international.title: Pathway to international play
international.text: Rankings are relevant for selecting players for international competitions, European and World championships, and other official tournaments organized by FIP and FEPA.

status.title: Build your sporting status
status.text: By taking part, players become part of the Federation's official competition system and can build their sporting status through recognized national and international competitions.

regulations.title: Regulations for the National Padel Championship
regulations.intro: The official propositions of the Padel Federation of Macedonia (MPF) governing the National Padel Championship.

meta.label: Categories
meta.value: Men's pairs / Women's pairs / Mixed pairs

blocks.text: The National Padel Championship (hereinafter: the Championship) is an official competition organized by the Padel Federation of Macedonia (MPF) in accordance with the Program for the Development of Padel in Macedonia.
The competition is open — all pairs (men's, women's, mixed) registered in accordance with these regulations are entitled to take part, with no limit on the number of registered participants.
The competition is held with a dual classification:

items: General winner — regardless of club membership (open to all participants)
Club ranking — exclusively for players who are members of clubs registered with the MPF

blocks.text: The technical organizer of the First National Padel Championship is Padel Club Kumanovo, which provides:

items: The courts for holding the competition
Referees and technical staff
The required equipment (balls, nets, scoreboard)
Administrative support for registration and the draw
Medical personnel — defibrillator and first aid

blocks.text: The technical organizer is obliged to provide a minimum of 2 courts for matches to be held simultaneously.
3.1 General competition
All players (minimum 16 years old) are entitled to take part in the general competition, provided they:

items: Complete the registration form by the registration deadline at the latest
Pay the entry fee
Sign a statement accepting the competition rules

blocks.text: 3.2 Club competition
All pairs in which BOTH players are members of the same club registered with the MPF automatically take part in the club ranking. The club must have paid its membership fee for the current year.
A club may register an unlimited number of pairs. The results of all of the club's pairs count toward the club standings (points system — see Article 7).

If the number of registered pairs in a given category is fewer than 4 (four), the organizing committee reserves the right to merge it with another category or to cancel it, in which case participants will have their entry fees refunded.
5.1 Registration deadline
Entries are submitted exclusively via the official MPF online form or by e-mail to: padelmkd@gmail.com
Final registration deadline: 7 (seven) days before the competition is held.
Entries received after the deadline will not be accepted unless the organizing committee decides otherwise.
5.2 Entry fee
Payment is made to the account of the technical organizer. After payment, the payment confirmation is submitted together with the entry.
The entry fee is non-refundable after the registration deadline, except in the case of an injury confirmed by medical documentation.
6.1 Format
The competition format depends on the number of registered pairs per category and is determined after registration closes:

head: No. of pairs
Format
rows: Group stage (1 or 2 groups) + direct elimination (semifinal + final)
2–4 groups with a group stage + round of 16 / quarterfinal / final

blocks.text: 6.2 Rules of play
The competition is played according to the official rules of the International Padel Federation (FIP), with the following local provisions:

items: Matches up to the semifinal are played to 2 winning sets, with a tie-break in the third set (10 points)
Semifinal and final: 2 winning sets; at 1:1, the third set is played to 10 points with no advantage
Balls: official FIP-approved balls — provided by the technical organizer
Warm-up: 5 minutes on court before the match
Lateness: a pair more than 10 minutes late loses 1 set; more than 20 minutes — the match

blocks.text: 7.1 General winner
The general winner per category is the pair that wins the final match. The placement is determined as follows:

items: 1st place: Winner of the final
2nd place: Finalist
Further placement: according to the elimination stage reached

blocks.text: 7.2 Club ranking
The club ranking is based on the points won by all of the club's pairs in the general competition:

The club standing is determined by the total sum of points of all the club's pairs, across all categories. In the event of a tie in points, the club with more pairs in a higher stage takes precedence.
The results achieved at the State Championship will be recorded by the Padel Federation of Macedonia and will serve as the basis for forming the official national ranking list of players.

The national ranking list will be used for seeding at competitions, the selection of national team line-ups and participation in international competitions and championships organized by FIP and FEPA, in accordance with the Federation's applicable rules and criteria.

items: General winner (per category): Trophy + Medals + Official MPF diploma
2nd place: Medals + Official MPF diploma
3rd place: Medals + Official MPF diploma
Club winner: Cup + MPF diploma

blocks.text: Cash prizes will be determined if the number of registered pairs exceeds the threshold of 30 pairs in total. The decision is made by the MPF Management Board after registration closes.
The competition is led by a Chief Referee appointed by the MPF. The referees for individual matches are provided by the technical organizer.
9.1 Protests

items: A protest may be filed by the captain of the pair (one of the two players)
The protest is submitted in writing to the Chief Referee immediately after the match ends or during the break (not during a point)
The decision of the Chief Referee is final on the day of the competition
An appeal to the MPF Disciplinary Committee may be filed within 48 hours after the competition ends — with supporting documentation

blocks.text: All participants, coaches and accompanying persons are obliged to respect the MPF Code of Conduct.

items: Warning (yellow card): for inappropriate behavior
Penalty point (orange card): repeated inappropriate behavior
Disqualification (red card): a serious offense, physical incident or insults

blocks.text: A disqualified pair is not entitled to a refund of the entry fee and may be suspended from MPF competitions.

items: Each participant takes part at their own responsibility and risk
A medical certificate of fitness for sports competition is recommended
The technical organizer is obliged to provide medical personnel on site
The MPF is not responsible for injuries occurring during the competition
Holding private health insurance is recommended

blocks.text: These regulations were adopted by the Management Board of the Padel Federation of Macedonia and are binding on all participants.
All matters not covered by these regulations are decided by the Organizing Committee in accordance with the rules of the MPF and FIP.
For all questions and additional information, please contact:

items: E-mail: padelmkd@gmail.com
Web: www.padelfederation.mk
